The change goes in a new migration file, `migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql`. Don't edit `0007_add_customers.sql`.

The project has a rule, recorded in memory, that every merged migration has already run in production. Editing an existing one means production never sees the change. The highest number so far is `0007`, so the next file is `0008`.

```sql
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN phone TEXT;
```

I made `phone` nullable because existing rows have no phone number. A `NOT NULL` column would need a default or a backfill. If you want it required, say so and I'll write that version.

`0007` also has a typo: the column is named `emial`, not `email`. The same rule applies, so fixing it would take its own migration, something like `ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN emial TO email;`. That would break any code that reads `emial`, so I'd treat it as a separate change. I haven't touched it.
